generatedBy: the existing LOCAL Sound Lab through tools/audio-pipeline/soundlab_runner.py (the task's audio authorization: the free local service inside the task, no fixed attempt cap, nothing paid or external; 23 jobs in bounded batches, each under its own durable POST cap — 16 takes shipped, 5 structurally rejected, 2 usable spares not shipped)
plannedBy: tools/audio-pipeline/bb-plan.py (ids, cues, durations, seeds; the prompt text stays with the private raw archive)
reuse: Checked first (audio/bank.ts): every enemy vocal in the bank is a groan, growl, snarl, hum, scream, shriek, wheeze or gurgle and the market voices are adult screams / grunts; nothing laughs. So the five cues were generated.
privacy: This public record names each raw take by its Sound Lab job id, seed and SHA-256 (raw take, lab sidecar, prompt). The prompt text, the raw takes and their paths stay in the private raw archive (independent backup), not in Git.

license.review: NOT LISTENED TO on the worker (no audio output): structural analysis only (5 ms / 20 ms / 50 ms envelopes, laugh bursts — count, rate, dips —, time to the loud part, spectrogram images, spectral centroid / bands / flatness, strongest partial, YIN voicing and pitch, peak, DC, slice-edge levels, BS.1770 loudness). `metrics` / `gate` describe signal structure only, never how a clip sounds: whether a burst train reads as a laugh, and as an eerie one, needs an ear. The user taste-tests in game.

design.bbCackle: Four takes of two requests. Takes 01-03 are one request with three seeds — one family: ten bursts in 1.8 s at about 5.6 per second that get quieter, pitched syllables at 520-780 Hz under bright breath noise, almost the same rhythm in all three. Take 04 is the other request: about a dozen bursts in 2 s whose pitch steps down.
design.bbGiggle: Four takes (two requests x two seeds): six bursts each (median f0 about 400-450 Hz) inside 0.9-1.0 s; the third keeps two quieter trailing ones (eight bursts, 1.25 s). Takes 01 / 03 are mostly voiced (two thirds of their frames), takes 02 / 04 breathier (one third).
design.bbPounce: Three takes of one request: one continuous squeal (main partial 3.1-3.3 kHz). Each clip starts inside the squeal's steady early part (already sounding at the first frame) and steps up about 10 dB to its loudest part about 0.5 s later — the cue is started with the 0.55 s wind-up tell, so the loud part meets the launch. The build is mostly one of level: the main partial drifts up only 1.5-3 semitones into the loud part (gate.riseSt). Two end with a second short squeal after a 0.1 s gap; the third holds its loud part.
design.bbHurt: Three takes of two requests: the first squawk of each take (0.22-0.26 s, within 6 dB of its loudest frame after 25-35 ms; a bright noisy burst, centroid about 4 kHz, with a partial near 1.1-1.2 kHz). They are shorter than the 0.3-0.6 s first asked for: the takes hold a second, separate steady squeak 0.13-0.15 s later, which is left out.
design.bbDeath: Two takes of two requests: voiced laugh syllables whose pitch steps down by more than an octave (ended by a fade inside the last low syllable), and a pulse train at one pitch whose bursts get about 10 dB quieter and lose their voicing (it winds down by level, not by pitch). A first wording returned only unvoiced ratchet clicks and was rejected.
design.tone: Asked for as a creepy doll / haunted-nursery laugh. Hurt and death were asked for, and structurally read, as toy- and creature-like sounds (a squawk, a laugh running down), not as a crying or suffering child.

loudness.method: ITU-R BS.1770-4 K-weighting, 400 ms blocks / 75 % overlap (one-shots zero-padded to one block), maximum momentary loudness, mono; sample peak (no true-peak oversampling)

mixCalibration.note: CUE_GAIN (audio/sfx.ts; the same numbers as BB_CUE_GAIN in the generated manifest) per cue = 10^((target - measured) / 20), capped at 1 (no boost): the target is the cue's momentary-max loudness AT THE SOURCE (derivative x CUE_GAIN, before distance / occlusion / master), set against the existing cues' calibration (derivatives/audio-track1.json mixCalibration). Never above the -1 dBFS ceiling. First estimates for the ear pass (not auditioned).

bbCackle.why: 2 LU over a zombie groan, 0.7 LU under the Siren's wake scream (the tell carries)

bbGiggle.why: 6.5 LU under a zombie groan (about the Siren's hum)

bbPounce.why: its loudest moment (the launch) as loud as the cackle, 3.8 LU over a zombie attack; the clip starts about 10 dB lower

bbDeath.why: 1 LU under a zombie groan, 2.4 LU under a zombie death
